segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Non-identical or fraternal twins come from two separate eggs and share half their genes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: More uncommon are identical twins who come from a single fertilised egg and share 100% of their genes.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: As humans, we're fascinated by twins.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: When people discover that someone's a twin, they start asking all kinds of questions.

segments.speaker: Beth

segments.text: Yeah, it is nice. There's never that fear because you're going through school together.

segments.speaker: Anand Jagatia
segments.text: You're sometimes in the same class together. You're making friends together.

segments.speaker: Anand Jagatia
segments.text: So all of those milestones of childhood in some ways are made easier for twins.

segments.speaker: Anand Jagatia
segments.text: But then the older you get, the more you realise how much people really think of you as a twin rather than as an individual.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Twins go through many childhood milestones together.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: A milestone is an important stage of development, so a childhood milestone could be something like your first day at school.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But being a twin isn always plain sailing an idiom meaning easy and problem Many twins find it hard to establish their own identity as a separate and unique individual

segments.speaker: Beth
